issues.title: Global well-posedness initial-data scope

failure_location.quote: Under the above assumptions on $V,W,\sigma$ and any $\mu_0\in L^1_+(\Omega)$, there exists a unique variational solution $\mu(t)$ of \eqref{eq:mckean_vlasov_repeat}.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem quantifies over every nonnegative unit-mass L1 datum. However, the regularity in def:varsol_repeat implies a continuous representative in L2 at the initial time, so equality with the initial datum forces the datum itself to belong to L2. Normalized L1 densities outside L2 are admissible under the old statement, making its input scope incompatible with its solution contract.
issues.overall_effect: Global well-posedness is not established in the advertised variational class for rough L1 probability densities. The old exponential-convergence proposition likewise cannot rely on that solution theory throughout its stated finite-entropy data class.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict thm:wellposed to nonnegative unit-mass initial data in L2(Ω), with the initial condition understood through the L2 trace. On the same repair route, restrict thm:expconv to finite-relative-entropy initial data that also belong to L2(Ω), retaining its conclusion and decay rate for that common class.
issues.why_classification: This is a contained hypothesis correction requiring no new proof architecture, and comparable well-posedness and convergence results survive. It is not minor because it withdraws the expressly advertised and natural L1-only data regime, including finite-entropy densities outside L2; that is a meaningful but limited loss rather than removal of the results.

issues.title: Exponential-convergence prefactor
issues.failure_explanation: The proposition claims exponential L1 convergence, but its prefactor is the undefined spatial norm of the full time-space function mu(·,·). It is neither the initial distance nor another specified time-independent quantity, so the displayed formula does not express the claimed decay from the initial condition.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition does not provide a usable quantitative decay estimate as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the undefined prefactor by the initial spatial distance, giving ‖μ(t,·)−μ̄‖L1 ≤ ‖μ0−μ̄‖L1 e^(−αt).
issues.why_classification: The spatial L1 convention, the immediately specified initial datum, and the form of the decay estimate uniquely identify the first dot in μ(·,·) as the initial time 0. This is a transcriptional correction that requires no change to the argument or guarantee.

issues.title: Unsupported reality of the nonlocal operator's spectrum

failure_location.quote: We concludes the proof because $\Hcal$ is bounded from below given that it is the sum of a bounded operator $\Psi + \mathcal{K}$ with a bounded from below operator $-\Delta$.

issues.failure_explanation: The perturbation results cited in the old proof preserve compact resolvent, not self-adjointness or reality of the spectrum. The displayed kernel of K is not shown symmetric. The inference is invalid in general: for example, adding the bounded matrix [[0,-1],[1,0]] to the self-adjoint matrix diag(0,1) produces the complex eigenvalues $(1\pm i\sqrt{3})/2$. Thus boundedness or a lower real-part bound does not establish the proposition's real-spectrum conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition overstates the spectral structure. Its useful compact-resolvent and finite-multiplicity conclusions remain available, and later arguments that use only those weaker conclusions are not affected by this root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate prop:pure-spectrum so that the spectrum consists of isolated, possibly complex eigenvalues of finite algebraic multiplicity with modulus tending to infinity. Remove the inference that a bounded, potentially non-self-adjoint perturbation makes the spectrum real, while retaining the established compact-resolvent conclusions.
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and leaves a recognizably comparable discrete-spectrum proposition, with no affected downstream result requiring reality. Nevertheless, replacing a real-spectrum guarantee by a possibly complex spectrum is a substantive, limited weakening rather than a routine same-guarantee correction, so the issue is moderate rather than minor.

issues.title: Wrong spectral half-plane in the finiteness proof

failure_location.quote: It follows that there are finitely many eigenvalues $\mu \in \sigma(\Hcal)$ such that $\Re(\mu) \le -\delta$

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The spectrum of the operator $\Hcal$ is the negative of the spectrum of the operator $\Lcal$

issues.failure_explanation: Writing $\eta=-\lambda$ gives $\Re(\lambda)\ge-\delta$ if and only if $\Re(\eta)\le\delta$. The old proof proves finiteness only for the smaller region $\Re(\eta)\le-\delta$ and then incorrectly infers the stated result. Its preceding bounded-imaginary-part and modulus-divergence argument does yield finiteness below the correct threshold once the sign is fixed.
issues.overall_effect: Until corrected, the finiteness of modes requiring control is not proved, leaving the Hautus argument and the subsequent Riccati and nonlinear-stabilization chain unestablished.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the proof set η=−λ and use Re(λ)≥−δ if and only if Re(η)≤δ, replacing the erroneous threshold −δ by δ. The preceding bounds on the imaginary parts and divergence of |η| then imply that only finitely many such η exist, restoring the lemma and the guarantee used by every listed dependent result.
issues.why_classification: The old proof makes a genuine invalid sign inference, so this is not merely typographical. However, the correct half-plane is forced by the stated spectral relation, and a one-line routine correction using estimates already proved establishes exactly the original lemma without weakening or additional machinery.

issues.title: Control-shape regularity and the control-operator interface

failure_location.quote: where $\Nop_j : H^1(\Omega, \bar\mu^{-1}) \to L^2(\Omega, \bar\mu^{-1})$ is defined as $\Nop_j \mu \coloneqq \nabla \cdot (\mu \nabla \alpha)$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where each $\alpha_j\in H^1(\Omega, \bar\mu^{-1})$ is a prescribed {\em shape function}

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that every advertised $H^1$ shape defines an operator $\Nop_j:H^1\to L^2$ by $\nabla\cdot(\mu\nabla\alpha_j)$. The old assumptions establish only $\mu,\alpha_j\in H^1$. Choosing $\mu\equiv1$ and a periodic $\alpha_j\in H^1\setminus H^2$ makes the output $\Delta\alpha_j$, which is not in L2. Thus the old source supports at most a distributional expression, not the claimed L2-valued operator; the stronger regularity in the latest source is materially necessary for that interface.
issues.overall_effect: The generic controlled and abstract formulations are not L2-valued for the full advertised shape class. The later elliptic construction may produce smoother shapes, so no formal theorem is listed as dependent on this generic overclaim.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Throughout the generic controlled formulation, require each shape αj to lie in W^{1,∞}(Ω)∩W^{2,p}(Ω), with p=max{d,2+ε}. Then ∇μ·∇αj and μΔαj belong to L2 for μ∈H1 by Hölder and Sobolev embedding, so Njμ=div(μ∇αj) genuinely defines Nj:H1→L2.
issues.why_classification: This is a contained, source-supported repair that preserves the L2 control architecture and applies to the smoother shapes produced by the later construction. It is not minor because it excludes the substantial advertised class of H1-only shapes, not merely an exceptional degeneracy. The smooth-shape formulation remains recognizably comparable, so no serious loss or global reconstruction is required.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: where each $\alpha_j\in W^{1,\infty}(\Omega) \cap W^{2,p}(\Omega)$ is a prescribed {\em shape function}

issues.title: Fredholm solvability condition

failure_location.quote: Therefore, the equation is solvable if and only if $\varphi_j \notin \operatorname{span}\{ \sqrt{\bar\mu} \}$, or equivalently, $\psi_j \notin \operatorname{span}\{ \bar\mu \}$, which is true by \autoref{remark:kernel_L0}.

issues.failure_explanation: For a self-adjoint Fredholm operator, solvability requires the right-hand side to be perpendicular to the kernel. A vector may fail to lie in the kernel's span while still having a nonzero component along it, so the old 'not in the span' equivalence is false. Here remark:kernel_L0 actually gives the stronger orthogonality of the relevant zero-mean eigenfunctions, which is the condition the proof must use.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the proof does not establish existence of the prescribed control shapes, leaving the Hautus conclusion and the subsequent Riccati and local-stabilization chain unsupported until the relation is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false non-membership condition by the Fredholm orthogonality condition. Explicitly use ψj∈X0 to obtain ⟨ψj,μ̄⟩_{μ̄^{-1}}=∫Ωψj=0 and, by unitarity, φj perpendicular to √μ̄. The elliptic shape equation is then solvable and the Hautus and listed downstream arguments proceed unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The proof contains a genuine false equivalence, but the old source already states the stronger zero-mean orthogonality needed to correct it. A short, routine substitution restores the same theorem and its entire affected chain without a new lemma, construction, or weakening.

issues.title: Incorrect full-space extension of the reduced Riccati equation

failure_location.quote: where equation~\eqref{eq:riccati_reduced} is posed directly on the zero-mean subspace, while \eqref{eq:riccati_full} is its extension to the full space.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that eq:riccati_full is an extension equivalent to the reduced Riccati equation. The old decomposition has complement $\operatorname{im}(\Qcal)=\operatorname{span}\{\bar\mu\}$, while $1 1^*$ has range in the constant functions and is not that complement for a nonconstant target. Moreover, extending the reduced generator requires $\Lcal\Pcal$ and its adjoint $\Pcal^*\Lcal^*$; the uncompressed old terms retain unwanted mass-component couplings. Thus the displayed equation and lift do not support the claimed equivalence.
issues.overall_effect: The ancillary full-space Riccati representation and its family of lifted solutions are not established. The reduced Riccati equation on the zero-mean space and the feedback subsequently used in prop:ARE remain unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Form the full-space Riccati equation with the compressed generator L P+δP and adjoint P*L*+δP*. Lift a reduced solution as Π=P*Π0P+γQ rather than P*Π0P+γ11*, and verify in the P⊕Q block decomposition that restriction and lifting are inverse constructions and that B*Q=0.
issues.why_classification: The old formulas are mathematically wrong rather than transcriptionally malformed, but standard local block-operator bookkeeping corrects both the generator and complementary block. The equivalent full-space representation and unchanged reduced feedback survive with no mathematical loss and no nontrivial new architecture.

issues.title: Riccati optimality based on a transformed cost with the wrong inner product
issues.failure_explanation: The Riccati argument supports optimality for the weighted state cost on $\Space_0$. Algebraically, $z=e^{\delta t}y$ gives $e^{2\delta t}\langle y,\Mcal y\rangle_{\bar\mu^{-1}}=\langle z,\Mcal z\rangle_{\bar\mu^{-1}}$. The old transformed problem instead uses the globally defined unweighted bracket, so prop:ARE's claimed optimal feedback is tied to a different objective than the one actually derived.
issues.overall_effect: The optimal-control interpretation in prop:ARE is inconsistent as written. Its existence and semigroup-stability conclusions, and the later stabilization argument using those conclusions, remain intact under the uniquely intended weighted reading.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the weighted inner product in eq:cost_transformed, replacing ⟨z,Mz⟩ by ⟨z,Mz⟩_{L2(Ω,μ̄^{-1})}, and state optimality for that weighted transformed cost.
issues.why_classification: The original weighted cost and the scalar change z=e^{δt}y uniquely force the weighted inner product after transformation. The isolated missing subscript does not alter any inference, Riccati equation, or stability conclusion and is therefore transcriptional.
